description: J.P. Morgan AI Research offers a set of synthetic datasets built to support research on artificial intelligence in financial services where real data cannot be shared. They include anti-money-laundering traces of legitimate and money-laundering clients' actions such as opening accounts and making transfers, customer journey events across mobile, web and ATM channels, market execution data, payments data for fraud detection with normal and fraudulent transactions injected at set probabilities, synthetic documents for layout recognition, and simulated equity market data. They are produced by the AI Research group of JPMorganChase, several by running an AI planning-execution simulator or agent-based generators calibrated against real data. The datasets are generic, not tied to real places. They are available free for non-commercial use on request by email, each under its original licence; those marked on the page are Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0. Caveats: data are synthetic, so realism depends on the generator, commercial use is barred, and the page does not list file sizes or formats. For simulation it supplies benchmark event streams for agent-based models of payment fraud, money laundering and customer behaviour, and a documented method for generating and validating synthetic financial data. It is related to the AMLSim record in this catalogue, an open-source simulator of money-laundering transactions.
